name: dev sermon chat suite
description: Ten grokbot1 chats used to check sermon-note influence on the dev server. Run one session per chat, in order, with a pause between turns so retrieval and generation do not pile up. Each chat asks for sermon notes, a direct question, or a biblical narrative, then two follow-ups.

turns: Create sermon notes on marriage as a blood covenant. What does Pastor Don actually teach a husband and wife to do?
What should a husband practice this week from that teaching?
Which part of that answer came from the sermon notes rather than Ephesians 5 in general?
Tell the story of David and Goliath the way the sermon notes teach it. What is the point of the story?
What was David's real advantage when he faced Goliath?
How should a believer apply that story when they are afraid of something bigger than they are?
What do the sermon notes teach about tithing? Is giving worship or an obligation?
Is the tithe the same thing as a freewill offering in those notes?
What do the notes say a person should do if they feel they cannot afford to give?
Create sermon notes on why a believer should receive the Holy Spirit. Stay with what the notes teach.
What do the notes say the Spirit does when a believer prays?
What happens if someone wants the Spirit's power but will not obey?
Explain the parable of the prodigal son from the sermon notes. Who is the father, and what does he do?
What do the notes say about the older brother?
How should a church treat someone who comes back after walking away?
According to the sermon notes, can a Christian drink alcohol?
Do those notes treat communion wine as the same issue?
What should a parent tell a teenager who asks if one drink is fine?
Walk through Moses and the Red Sea the way the sermon notes tell it.
What did God tell the people to do when the sea was still in front of them?
How do the notes apply a dead-end situation to an ordinary believer?
Create a pastoral outline from the sermon notes for restoring a broken relationship inside the church.
What is the first step the notes say the offended person must take?
When, if ever, do the notes say the whole church should be told?
Tell the story of the good Samaritan from the sermon notes. What is the teaching point?
Why did the priest and the Levite pass by, according to the notes?
Who is my neighbor in that teaching, and what should I do this week?
Create sermon notes on hope for someone who is sick or grieving. Use what the notes actually say.
Do the notes treat God's silence during illness as absence?
What practical step do the notes give a person who is in pain?
